items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: With the Delta Four for this recording session, there was ... a singer named Dell St. John.

ctx.x: The fourth of April, I recorded with Joe Marsala and his Delta Four, a session that was supervised by Leonard Feather. I had met Leonard in Paris where he came a few times to listen to certain jazz musicians as he was a critic of jazz music and wrote for the English musical paper 'Melody Maker'. Leonard had gone to New York at the beginning or shortly after the war started in 1939 and was later to become one of the editors of 'Down Beat', which was the best jazz magazine in the States at one time. Leonard also…

With the Delta Four for this recording session, there was Pete Brown, Carmen Mastren, Gene Traxler and a singer named Dell St. John. Joe Marsala played clarinet and was well known by the white jazz musicians all over the States. Pete Brown, I had known for years and the first time I heard him play was at the Savoy with a relief band. He played alto sax and his style was very original. He played very staccato in an abrupt, disconnected manner which was opposed to legato and was the swingingest alto player I ever…

Carmen was also well known in the jazz field as was Traxler and they were both musicians with plenty of class. Dell St. John was a Negro girl who had a fine voice and could sing the blues in a style that was strictly Dell.
